info.name: searxng
info.description:
SearXNG metasearch endpoints. Direct host publish — no LiteLLM pass-through, no auth. Set the collection variable `searxng` (default http://localhost:8009 = PORT_SEARXNG). On ai_shared this is `http://searxng:8080`. See ai/searxng/SEARXNG.md for the operator guide.

Rate limiting: `server.limiter: false` in ai/searxng/settings.yml, so the built-in IP rate limiter is OFF and server-to-server callers (Open WebUI, curl, this collection) are not throttled. limiter.toml exists only to silence a startup warning. If you flip limiter back on, /search calls without the expected browser headers will start returning 429 — see https://docs.searxng.org/admin/searx.limiter.html.

Output formats: `search.formats: [html, json]` in settings.yml. Upstream defaults omit `json` — the override is what lets Open WebUI (and the JSON requests below) consume results. Omitting `format=json` returns the HTML search results page.

Engines: this deployment inherits the upstream default engine set (google, bing, duckduckgo, wikipedia, etc.) via `use_default_settings: true`. Nothing is disabled in settings.yml.

variable.description: SearXNG base URL. Host publish is 8009 (PORT_SEARXNG in .env); on ai_shared it's http://searxng:8080. No auth — direct access. See ai/searxng/SEARXNG.md for the port/network topology.

request.description: Liveness probe. Returns plain text `OK` (Content-Type: text/plain) when the internal Flask app is up. This is exactly the endpoint the Docker healthcheck in docker-compose.searxng.yml polls every 30s via `urllib.request.urlopen`. Cheap — no upstream engine calls.

query.description: Output format. Required for programmatic use — omit to get the HTML results page instead. Enabled via `search.formats: [html, json]` in ai/searxng/settings.yml.

request.description:
Programmatic search entrypoint. Returns JSON: `{query, number_of_results, results: [{url, title, content, engine, ...}], answers, corrections, infoboxes, suggestions, unresponsive_engines}`. This is the exact URL shape Open WebUI hits (`SEARXNG_QUERY_URL=http://searxng:8080/search?q=<query>&format=json`) — see SEARXNG.md § Wiring into Open WebUI.

Fan-out: every call spawns fresh requests to all enabled upstream engines (google, bing, duckduckgo, etc. from the upstream default set via `use_default_settings: true`). Latency is dominated by the slowest engine. If `results` is empty, upstream engines all failed — check `docker logs searxng` and inspect `unresponsive_engines`.

Rate limit: none, because `server.limiter: false` in settings.yml. Public egress IP may still get rate-limited by Google/Bing themselves — that surfaces as engines dropping into `unresponsive_engines`, not as a 429 from SearXNG.

query.description: Comma-separated category filter. Upstream defaults include: general, images, videos, news, map, music, it, science, files, social media. Only engines tagged with a matching category run — narrows fan-out and lowers latency.

request.description:
Category-filtered search. Same JSON response shape as the plain `/search` call. Category names come from the upstream engine catalogue — see https://docs.searxng.org/user/configured_engines.html for the full mapping of engines to categories.

Use this when a caller only wants (say) news or images and the untargeted fan-out would waste latency on irrelevant engines.

query.description: IETF language tag (e.g. `en`, `en-US`, `de`, `fr`, `all`). Overrides `search.default_lang` in ai/searxng/settings.yml — which is empty here, meaning per-request must supply the tag if a language bias is wanted. `all` disables language biasing.

request.description: Language-biased search. Same JSON response shape. Per-engine handling differs — Google/Bing use it as a soft bias, Wikipedia uses it to pick the language subdomain. Combine with `categories` freely.

Human-facing search UI. Returns the full HTML landing page (Content-Type: text/html) — a search box, engine toggles, preferences link. NOT a JSON API. Use this only to eyeball the deployment from a browser (SEARXNG.md § Quick start). For programmatic use, hit `/search?…&format=json` instead.

Deployment introspection. Returns JSON describing the running instance's configuration: enabled engines (with their categories, timeouts, shortcuts), enabled categories, supported result formats, safe_search level, default language, autocomplete backend, plugin list, brand info. Useful to confirm the settings.yml overrides actually loaded — e.g. `formats` should list both `html` and `json` here.

Exposed by default upstream and not disabled in ai/searxng/settings.yml. Read-only, no side effects.

Engine performance dashboard. Returns HTML (Content-Type: text/html) tabulating per-engine response times, error rates, and result counts since the container started. Useful when `/search` returns thin results — identify which engines are timing out or failing before touching config.

JSON variant: append `?format=json` (some releases; not guaranteed). For a machine-readable error breakdown, `/stats/errors` returns HTML with a similar table.

Exposed by default upstream and not disabled in ai/searxng/settings.yml.
